historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly separates reachability from physical connection, but blind scanning on a PDB management bus can touch PMBus controllers, hot-swap devices, EEPROMs or power controls and an ACK does not prove the intended PDB identity.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Adds BMC/OOB ownership, exact PDB controller and device map, safe read allowlist, operator photos, power/rail stability evidence and vendor recovery.

original_test_intent: Prove that the BMC's logical I2C-9 path is physically connected to the intended power distribution board and can safely identify every required PDB management device without changing rail, hot-swap, protection or EEPROM state.
original_method: Bind I2C-9 to the exact BMC controller/adapter/mux/channel and PDB connector; identify PDB assembly/serial/revision and its expected PMBus/I2C devices, 7-bit addresses and read-safe manufacturer/identity registers; classify clear-on-read and prohibited control/status operations; have an operator inspect/photograph the BMC-PDB connection and confirm stable rail/load state; preserve BMC/PDB/power baselines; execute only vendor-approved read-only discovery/identity transactions; correlate complete responses with the PDB oracle and stop on any bus or power anomaly without writes/reset/retry.
manual_activity: An operator verifies PDB assembly identity and BMC-PDB connector seating under the approved service state, records photos and monitors rail/power stability; software cannot replace these checks.
required_inputs: Logical I2C-9 to BMC controller/adapter/mux/channel/PDB connector map
PDB PN/serial/revision and expected device/address list with safe identity registers, data formats and values
Clear-on-read, PMBus control, hot-swap, EEPROM and protection-register prohibition list plus vendor-approved read method
Physical service state, load/rail limits, bus/power error acceptance, aborts and recovery
safety_requirements: Use only the approved BMC/OOB PDB management path and verify stable power before access
Do not use generic quick-write scans or read unknown/clear-on-read status; never issue PMBus control, EEPROM or protection writes
Preserve BMC/PDB fault and rail evidence before and after the check
Stop on rail excursion, hot-swap/protection event, bus timeout/stuck state, arbitration storm, unexpected device or BMC/PDB instability
agent_execution_scope: Validate exact PDB assembly/topology and device/register allowlist plus physical/service interlocks
After operator confirmation, collect only approved read-only PDB identity and bus/power-health evidence
Report every missing/unexpected/mismatched response without changing power state
Do not guess adapter/address/register, run a generic scan, write/clear controls, reset BMC/PDB or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve I2C-9 controller/mux/PDB path, PDB assembly and expected device oracle
Approve safe registers/commands, clear-on-read/control prohibitions, physical service state, rail/error limits and recovery
Review physical, identity and power-health evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: i2cdetect/i2cget are not automatically safe for a live PDB and the literal `I2C-9` target is unverified; generic ACKs cannot establish PDB assembly or device identity.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the vendor-approved BMC/PDB read path on the mapped channel and query only allowlisted non-clear-on-read identity registers while preserving complete responses and synchronized rail/bus health.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC I2C-9 to PDB scope, AI_VR_I2C_bus9 bundle, and 10/10-minute allocation remain; PDB device/register values are not invented.

modernized_recommendation.status: HIGH POWER_SAFE HYBRID BMC PDB I2C FUNCTIONAL CHECK
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the physical PDB assembly and connector to a controller/mux-specific read allowlist, exclude all state-changing and clear-on-read operations, and correlate identity responses with rail/protection health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds PDB assembly identity, exact management topology, register side-effect analysis, power interlocks, operator evidence and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: An address map can ACK through the wrong board or device and does not show correct PDB revision or safe communication; photos cannot prove protocol identity.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: PDB buses may expose power controllers whose SMBus/PMBus commands can change rails, clear faults or trigger protection; even nominal reads can have side effects at selected registers.

project_override_considerations: A vendor BMC PDB inventory interface is preferable when it maps stable PDB identities and device health without raw bus access. Host-side or generic I2C enumeration and power telemetry alone do not prove this BMC I2C-9 path.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, authorization, PDB PN/serial/revision and operator connection photos
BMC controller/adapter/mux/channel/PDB connector map and service/load state
Expected PDB device/address plus approved identity register/value allowlist and prohibited-operation list
Exact approved commands and complete device identity response comparison
Pre/post PDB rail/protection/hot-swap state and BMC/I2C timeout/NACK/arbitration/stuck-bus evidence

review_improvement: Adds PDB assembly identity and power-safety semantics so generic probing cannot disturb a live power-distribution bus or falsely satisfy communication coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: A PDB management bus has a larger blast radius than ordinary inventory I2C because PMBus and hot-swap controllers can directly affect rails and fault latches. Bus enumeration is therefore not a harmless default. The evidence must bind the physical board and mux path to read-safe identity responses while proving power/protection state remained stable. Side-effect and clear-on-read analysis is required before even nominal read commands are allowed.
